subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging IGCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for Edexcel IGCSE Maths simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

learningObjectives.title: Sine and cosine rules, area = 1/2 ab sinC (Higher)
Surface area and volume of solids
Congruence and similarity (area k^2 / volume k^3)

questions.q: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: Interior angle sum = (6-2)x180 = 720 degrees. Divided by 6 sides = 120 degrees each.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explain: Exterior angles sum to 360 degrees, so number of sides = 360 / 40 = 9.

questions.q: The angle subtended at the centre of a circle is twice the angle subtended at the circumference from the same arc. If the angle at the circumference is 35 degrees, what is the angle at the centre?
questions.explain: Angle at centre = 2 x angle at circumference = 2 x 35 = 70 degrees.

questions.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is 105 degrees. What is the size of the opposite angle?
questions.explain: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180 degrees, so 180 - 105 = 75 degrees.

questions.q: The angle between a tangent to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of contact is always:
questions.explain: A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at a right angle, 90 degrees.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has the two shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: Hypotenuse = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 cm.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one shorter side 5 cm. What is the other shorter side?
questions.explain: Other side = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle the side opposite an angle is 5 cm and the hypotenuse is 10 cm. What is the angle (to the nearest degree)?
questions.explain: sin(angle) = opposite / hypotenuse = 5/10 = 0.5, so angle = sin^-1(0.5) = 30 degrees.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 40 degrees with an adjacent side of 8 cm. Which ratio finds the opposite side?
questions.explain: tan = opposite / adjacent, so opposite = adjacent x tan(angle) = 8 x tan40.

questions.q: You know two sides of a triangle and the angle BETWEEN them, and want the third side. Which rule do you use?
questions.explain: The cosine rule a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cosA is used when you have two sides and the included angle.

questions.q: A triangle has two sides of 6 cm and 10 cm with an included angle of 30 degrees. What is its area? (sin30 = 0.5)
questions.explain: Area = 1/2 ab sinC = 0.5 x 6 x 10 x sin30 = 0.5 x 60 x 0.5 = 15 cm^2.

questions.q: In triangle ABC, angle A = 40 degrees, angle B = 60 degrees and side a (opposite A) = 8 cm. Which sets up side b correctly using the sine rule?
questions.explain: Sine rule: a/sinA = b/sinB, so b = a x sinB / sinA = 8 x sin60 / sin40.

questions.q: To find the angle a diagonal of a cuboid makes with its base, you first need which length using Pythagoras?
options: The diagonal of the base rectangle
questions.explain: In 3D trig you first find the base diagonal, then use it as the adjacent side in a right-angled triangle with the vertical height.

questions.q: A cuboid has a base diagonal of 12 cm and vertical height 5 cm. What is the length of the space diagonal from bottom corner to top corner?
questions.explain: Space diagonal = sqrt(12^2 + 5^2) = sqrt(144 + 25) = sqrt(169) = 13 cm.

questions.q: A bearing is always measured...
options: Clockwise from North as a three-figure number
Clockwise from South as a two-figure number
Anticlockwise from North as a three-figure number
Anticlockwise from East as a two-figure number
questions.explain: Bearings are measured clockwise from North and always written with three figures, e.g. 075 degrees.

questions.q: A circle has radius 7 cm. Taking pi = 22/7, what is its area?
A sector has a radius of 6 cm and an angle of 90 degrees. What is its area? (Use pi = 3.14)
A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use pi = 3.14)
Two similar solids have a length scale factor of 3. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.explain: Volume scale factor = (length scale factor)^3 = 3^3 = 27, so the volumes are in ratio 27 : 1.

questions.q: Two similar shapes have a length scale factor of 4. The smaller area is 5 cm^2. What is the larger area?
questions.explain: Area scale factor = (length scale factor)^2 = 4^2 = 16, so larger area = 5 x 16 = 80 cm^2.
